title: Vanishing Gaussian tail mass
statement: For each natural number $q$, let $A_q$ be the proportion of points in the Boolean cube of dimension $d_q$ whose normalized Rademacher sum exceeds the Gaussian upper-tail quantile corresponding to mass $1/(q+2)$, where $d_q$ is the dimension chosen so that this proportion approximates that mass and its level-one Fourier weight approximates the square of the corresponding Gaussian boundary measure. Then $2A_q$ tends to $0$ as $q$ tends to infinity.
hypotheses_covered: The index $q$ ranges over the natural numbers.
For each $q$, the dimension $d_q$ is the chosen approximation dimension.
The approximated mass is $1/(q+2)$, with both mass and level-one Fourier-weight approximation conditions.
The sequence is indexed by $q$ tending to infinity.
